part2.question: Describe a time when you changed an important opinion of yours

segments.v: I want to talk about an opinion I changed last year. Before, I thought reading novels was a waste of time. I thought students should only read useful books, like books for exams. I didn't understand why my friends read novels. My aunt often wanted to lend me novels but I always said no. Last summer, I stayed at my grandparents' house and there was no Wi-Fi. I was bored so I read a novel from my aunt. It was about a family during the war. I liked it very much. After that, I read more novels. I learned many new words and I understood other people better. I felt a little embarrassed because I was wrong before. Now I think reading novels is very useful.
I'd like to talk about an opinion I changed about a year ago, in grade 10, about reading

grammar.band6: Error: “because I was wrong before” (because I'd been wrong / I'd been so dismissive).
grammar.band9: Conditional in reported view (if I was going to read, it should be…), “keep + V-ing”, past perfect (in a way no history lesson ever had), and gerund subject (Changing my mind taught me…).

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 error: “because I was wrong before” should be past perfect (“because I'd been wrong” / “I'd been so dismissive”). Band 9 explains the old opinion honestly, shows the turning point as a story, lists the benefits, and reflects on how opinions are formed.
